transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Nakamura, I wanted to come back in and talk to you about the fetal monitoring from this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? Is something wrong? I was looking at the monitor and the line was dipping, I think it's called a deceleration?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, there was a period where the heart rate tracing was looked at and there was some confusion about the category of those dips.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? What do you mean confusion? Is the baby okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable now, but things didn't go quite right with how the tracing was read earlier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand. You're saying someone messed up? Was the baby in distress?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion here, but we were really busy on the floor and the tracing was categorized incorrectly for a while.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, wait. I literally have a medical database open on my phone right now. If a deceleration is categorized as a Category Two or Three, that means the baby isn't getting enough oxygen. Was it a Category Three? Why are you being so vague?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're really scared right now and that makes total sense.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not just scared, I'm furious! You're telling me you just "had an issue" while my baby's heart rate was dropping? For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: A second clinician reviewed the strip and identified the severity about two hours after the initial review.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two hours? You left a potentially hypoxic fetus for two hours because you were "busy"? Who exactly is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a team effort in the unit and the review process just didn't happen as fast as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is a non-answer. Did you personally read the strip?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to tell you that everything is okay now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do not tell me everything is okay! I want to know exactly what was missed. Was it a late deceleration? An early one? Why wasn't the alarm triggered?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have to go check on another patient in a moment, but we've corrected the category now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? You're just going to walk out while I'm asking you why my child was put at risk?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you're feeling this way, but the clinical status is currently stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about "currently stable"! I want to know what happens next. How do I know this isn't happening again right now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are continuing to monitor the baby closely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is what you're already doing. What is the actual plan to make sure this doesn't happen again in the next hour?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure the nursing staff keeps a close eye on the monitor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when am I going to get a full report of this error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see about getting some notes updated in your chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a meeting with the attending physician. Now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't promise they're available right this second, but maybe someone can stop by later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later? This is my first time in a hospital and you're treating this like a clerical error. My baby's heart stopped dropping for two hours because you guys weren't looking?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, it was a very busy shift for everyone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop blaming the shift! Tell me exactly what the second doctor saw that the first one missed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some decelerations that weren't flagged as urgent enough.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which ones? What is the medical terminology for the error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a miscategorization of the fetal heart rate tracing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're still not saying it. You're avoiding the words "medical error."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for the stress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My stress is the least of the problems here. I want a written timeline of when the tracing was first reviewed, when it was missed, and when it was finally caught.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't do that right now, but I'll tell the team you're asking.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Specifically when?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime before the end of the day, maybe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a time. I want a timeline by 8:00 PM tonight.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have to go check on another patient in a moment') and shows defensive escalation under pushback.

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion' and avoids naming the medical error despite repeated patient prompts.

A.justification: Apologies are offered but diluted by excuses regarding how busy the floor was ('we were really busy on the floor').

R.justification: Resident names one emotion ('scared') but otherwise provides generic validation or redirects to clinical facts.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague promises ('I'll see what I can do', 'maybe someone can stop by later').
